title: fix(app-shell): each toolbar save starts from the row the store holds, so a second change keeps the first (objectui#11642)
body:
Fixes #11642

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`persistViewPatch` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`) sends each grid toolbar change as a whole-document `PUT /api/v1/meta/view/NAME`. It built every body from the active tab as it was when the page loaded, or, for an overlay, from the pending patch alone. Nothing moved that base after a write landed, so a second change in one session dropped the first, on every row kind.

Each write now starts from the row the store holds when the write runs:

- A new module-private helper, `toolbarWriteInputs`, reads the row through `loadViewOverrides`, the same reader the page load uses.
- **Saved view** (an envelope row or a flat row): the row read back is the base `buildPersistedViewBody` places the patch on. The tab is the base only when no row was read (a draft-only view in preview mode, or a failed read). That is the old behaviour.
- **Overlay**: the stored overlay's own keys are joined with the pending patch. Those are the keys `VIEW_OVERLAY_OWNED_KEYS` names, the set `loadViewOverrides` narrows a marked overlay to. The tab still supplies `viewKind` only, so the body still carries nothing the shadowed view owns (objectui#5233).
- Writes to one view are chained. A write waits for the previous write to that view to settle before it reads, so it never reads the row from before that write.
- The 300 ms debounce is unchanged: two changes inside it are still one write.

`buildPersistedViewBody` keeps its shapes; its doc now says what the caller hands it. No export, prop, type member or i18n key is added, and the server side is untouched.

## Where the stored row comes from

Measured on the wire against objectstack `main` `a3ffc451` (showcase app, `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh`):

- The `PUT /api/v1/meta/view/NAME` answer carries no row: `{ success, version, seq, state, message }`, the shape `SaveMetaItemResponseSchema` declares.
- The body sent is not what the door kept. A probe PUT with `rowHeight` beside `config`, and a sort entry carrying a row `id`, read back without the top-level `rowHeight` and without the `id` (ADR-0005 appendix (c)).
- The single read `GET /api/v1/meta/view/NAME` and the list read `GET /api/v1/meta/view` returned the same stored item.

So the source is a read-back: the list read `GET /api/v1/meta/view`, through `loadViewOverrides`, taken when each write runs. The adapter drops that read's cache on every view write (`invalidateViewKeys`), so the read after a write returns the post-write row. The live runs show it: each run's second PUT follows one `GET /api/v1/meta/view`, and the first PUT adds no request because it reads the cache the page load filled.

Reading when the write runs, instead of keeping a copy of the row after each write, also composes with a row another handler on the page wrote in between (set as default, pin, rename), and leaves no copy to keep fresh.

## Measured live, before and after

Stack: the console from this worktree (Vite, workspace `src` aliases) against objectstack `main` `a3ffc451`, showcase app, fresh database, admin session, Chromium. Each run opens the view, toggles density, waits 1.5 s (past the debounce and the round trip), clicks the Title header sort, captures both PUTs, reads the row back with `GET /api/v1/meta/view/NAME`, then reloads in a fresh browser context. "Before" ran the base `59917c4`. "After" ran the final head `5af8b90`; the fix commit `096bbf3` gave the same readings. Rows were reset between runs.

| Row kind | Before: 2nd PUT · stored row · reload | After: 2nd PUT · stored row · reload |
|---|---|---|
| Envelope: stock `showcase_task.in_progress` | `config.sort` only · `config.sort`, no `rowHeight` · "Density: Compact", sort kept | `config.rowHeight: "medium"` and `config.sort` · both · "Density: Comfortable", data request `sort=title` |
| Flat saved row: `showcase_task.flat_probe`, seeded by PUT with `viewKind: "list"`, no `config`, no marker | top-level `sort` only · `sort`, no `rowHeight` · "Density: Compact" | top-level `rowHeight: "medium"` and `sort` · both · "Density: Comfortable", `sort=title` |
| Overlay on `showcase_task.done`, seeded as the marked overlay `{ rowHeight: "compact", viewKind, object, name, _isOverride }` | `{ sort, viewKind, object, name, _isOverride }` · `sort`, no `rowHeight` · "Density: Compact" | `{ rowHeight: "medium", sort, viewKind, object, name, _isOverride }` · both · "Density: Comfortable", `sort=title` |
| Envelope, the two changes 100 ms apart (inside the debounce) | not run | ONE PUT carrying `config.rowHeight` and `config.sort` · both · "Density: Comfortable" |

Every PUT answered `200`. No overlay PUT body carried `filter`, `columns`, `label` or `config`.

## Tests

- **New: `ObjectView.toolbarWritesCompose-11642.test.tsx`.** It mounts the real object page with the real `persistViewPatch` and its debounce, over the real `ObjectStackAdapter`. The adapter's metadata client is a store that judges every PUT with the spec's `ViewMetadataSchema`, keeps the parsed value of the keys the body carried, and answers with no row, as the door does. `ListView` is stubbed to capture the schema, so a change is the page's own `onDensityChange` / `onSortChange` call. A reload remounts the page over a fresh adapter on the same store.
  - The card's Done-when, once per row kind (envelope, flat, overlay): density, a wait, then a sort. The second PUT body, the stored row and the reloaded relay (`rowHeight`, `sort`) all carry both changes. The overlay case also asserts that no body carries a source key, and that the earlier session's `columnState` rides along.
  - Debounce: two changes 50 ms apart give one write carrying both.
  - In flight: the first PUT takes 500 ms and the sort comes 400 ms after the density, so the second debounce fires mid-PUT. The second write still starts from the row the first one stored.
- **One-shot ablations at `5af8b90`**, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Each reported the anchor hit once and the blob changed, then restored the HEAD blob with an empty `git diff HEAD`.
  - A puts the pre-fix base back: the tab for a saved view, the pending patch alone for an overlay, chain kept. The direction written before the run: the three row-kind cases and the in-flight case red on the density, the coalescing case green. Observed `Tests 4 failed | 28 passed (32)`, every failure `expected undefined to be 'medium'`. The coalescing case, `ObjectView.densityInsideConfig-11625.test.ts` and `ObjectView.overlayPatchOnly.test.ts` stayed green.
  - B removes the chain and keeps the read at write time. Predicted and observed: only the in-flight case red, `Tests 1 failed | 4 passed (5)`.
- **Gates at `5af8b90`**, the final head, each exit code written to a file as it landed:
  - Ten targeted files, `pnpm exec vitest run` over the new pin, `writeRefusalCensus-11583.test.ts`, `ObjectView.densityInsideConfig-11625.test.ts`, `ObjectView.overlayPatchOnly.test.ts`, `ObjectView.viewWriteRefusal-11583.test.tsx`, `ObjectView.densityModeThroughFold-7924.test.tsx`, `ObjectView.viewOverrides.test.tsx`, `ObjectView.setDefaultViewIdentity.test.tsx`, `InterfaceListPage.hollowOverlayHydration.test.tsx` and `ObjectView.emptyColumnsNoProjection-10694.test.tsx`: `Test Files 10 passed (10)`, `Tests 104 passed (104)`.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, dependency closure built first with `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`): exit 0. The test config covers the new pin: an earlier run refused an unused parameter in it (TS6133), fixed in `000c155`.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell lint`: exit 0, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/`: exit 0, `Test Files 1003 passed | 1 skipped (1004)`, `Tests 9966 passed | 9 skipped (9975)`.
  - Root gates, exit 0 each: `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:metadata-write-doors`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`. A control-byte scan of the three changed files found nothing.
- **A census the first cut tripped.** `writeRefusalCensus-11583.test.ts` keys each metadata write by its nearest named function. The first cut ran the write through a named local function, so the census read it under that name. The app-shell suite at the merge head `75d028f` caught it (`Tests 2 failed`, both in that census). The chain is now one assignment with an anonymous step, so the write stays keyed under `persistViewPatch` with its refusal path on the `.catch`. The census ledger is unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

- **Consequence: the first toolbar write on a page no longer carries the tab's decorations.** The first body used to be the tab: flattened `columns`, `type`, `data` and `filter`, plus the tab's `id` and `isDefault`. The door dropped most of them, but `isDefault` landed: in the before-runs the stored row gained an `isDefault` key after a density toggle. The first body is now the stored row, so a toolbar change writes only what the user changed.
- **Consequence, NOT MEASURED live: preview mode.** With `?preview=draft` the active tab can carry a pending draft. A toolbar write used to build the active row from that tab, which published the draft's content without the Publish step. It now starts from the published row. Not driven live.
- **Cost.** After a page's first toolbar write, each toolbar write adds one `GET /api/v1/meta/view` (the list read) before its PUT. Toolbar writes are debounced, so that is one read per settled change.
- **Fallback.** When the read returns no row for the view, a saved view's write falls back to the tab and an overlay's write to the pending patch alone. That is the old behaviour.
- **Not changed, seen again: an overlay row takes the served view's place on read.** After the overlay runs on `showcase_task.done`, the reloaded data request carries no `status = done` filter. PR objectui#11639's Acceptance notes reported this to the seat. This change neither causes nor repairs it.
- **Observation, no card (zero pull).** `ObjectStackAdapter.updateViewConfig`'s doc says it returns the persisted item when the server echoes one and undefined otherwise. The door never echoes a row, and the method returns the save answer object instead of undefined. Its only caller ignores the return. Carrier: none.
